# Project Instructions (AGENTS.md)

This is the one instruction source for **every** AI coding assistant on this repo. It is authored
once here and fanned out to each tool's native location by the sync mechanism
(`agent-src/sync/sync.ps1`). The content below is tool-neutral; only a short preamble differs per
tool.

---

## 1. Documentation structure — the `agent/` wiki

This repo carries an AI-augmented knowledge base under `agent/` (a visible, committed folder — no
dot prefix). It is a **four-layer hybrid wiki**; the authoritative rules are in
[`agent/schema.md`](agent/schema.md).

```
agent/
├── README.md   overview + quickstart
├── index.md    catalog (categorised entry point) — regenerated by hso-wiki-lint
├── log.md      append-only chronological event stream (newest on top)
├── schema.md   folder + frontmatter + linter-invariant rules
│
├── raw/        IMMUTABLE sources (LLM reads, never writes) + external-source captures
├── _inbox/     transient drop zone (routed by hso-wiki-process-inbox)
├── wiki/       COMPILED, durable knowledge (system topics sop reference decisions digests people)
└── work/       PROJECT DELIVERABLES by phase (analysis specs design build testing deliverables)
```

**wiki vs work:** is this knowledge that outlives the project, or an artifact we are delivering?
Topics, ADRs, digests → `wiki/`. Specs, TDDs, test plans, deliverables → `work/`.

Product-tier knowledge (reusable methodology, platform patterns) is inherited live via the
`shared/` junction (e.g. `shared/dv/agent/wiki/…`). See the three tiers below.

---

## 2. Three tiers — product / project / personal

| Tier | Location | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| **Product** | inherited via `shared/dv/…` (gitignored junction) | Reusable methodology + platform knowledge, versioned centrally |
| **Project** *(this repo)* | `agent/…` | One client, one engagement — committed here |
| **Personal** | a separate per-human repo | One person's private working memory — never folded into this repo |

Promotion between tiers is deliberate (copy up, then delete from the lower tier) — nothing
auto-promotes. The `shared/` junction MUST be present for the inherited product tier to resolve; a
first-run guard (`agent-src/sync/check-shared.ps1 -Strict`) fails fast with a clear message when it
is absent, so a session never silently reads nothing.

---

## 3. Template-First principle (MANDATORY)

This repository is a **reusable template**. Behaviour and structure live as **editable blueprints**
that skills read and generate from — never as values hardcoded inside skill code.

- A change to what the tooling produces is a change to a **template file or a config blueprint**
  (`ProjectTemplate/PipelinesHelpers/config/*.json`), not an edit buried in a skill.
- **Neutral by construction.** No customer identity is baked into the reusable core. Use the tokens
  in [ADR-0003](docs/decisions/ADR-0003-naming-and-token-contract.md) (`HSO.Customer.*`,
  `hso_customer_`, `hso`, `PROJECTCODE`, `solutionPrefix`) — never a real customer name.
- **Generated files are never hand-edited.** `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`,
  `.claude/skills/`, and `.github/skills/` are outputs of `agent-src/sync/sync.ps1`. Edit the source
  under `agent-src/` (skills) or `AGENTS.md` (instructions), then re-run the sync.

### Reusable core vs project-specific skills

Skills are authored in two source trees and fanned out by the sync:

- `agent-src/skills/core/` — reusable, product-tier, customer-agnostic skills (grouped: `foundation
  dataverse server client pipelines delivery reference meta`). These round-trip to `shared/`.
- `agent-src/skills/project/` — engagement-specific skills (hardcoded pipeline IDs, client estate,
  ticket workflow). Never synced upstream.

`agent-src/sync/skills-manifest.json` records every skill's `scope` (core | project) and tool
targets. When creating a skill, choose its scope explicitly (`hso-skill-creator --scope
core|project`). **Rule:** a skill that names a client, a pipeline ID, an environment URL, or a sprint
convention is project-scoped until those are externalised to config.

## 4. Pre-Implementation Checklist (MANDATORY)

**BEFORE planning ANY implementation:**

1. **Read `agent/README.md` and `agent/index.md`** — the wiki entry point and catalog.
2. **Read `agent/wiki/system/`** — current system state, tech stack, component inventory, schema
   snapshots, and the TOPO map (`agent/wiki/system/solution-map.topo`).
3. **Read the relevant product-tier SOP(s)** under `shared/dv/agent/wiki/sop/**` (start at the topic
   anchor in `shared/dv/agent/wiki/topics/<subject>.md` to discover the right SOPs, references, ADRs,
   and skills).
4. **Read the component README** for specific implementation details.
5. **ONLY THEN** plan.

If you skip a step, STOP and complete it before continuing.

---

## 5. Triage FIRST — is it a bug, or the agreed/designed behaviour? (MANDATORY, every ticket)

**Before investigating or fixing ANY reported "issue", first check whether the described behaviour is
actually what was requested, agreed, or deliberately designed.** A large share of reports are not
bugs — the reporter simply did not know the system was agreed to work that way.

1. **Check the record** for a decision that the behaviour is intentional — search
   `agent/wiki/decisions/` (ADRs), `agent/work/specs/`, `agent/work/analysis/`,
   `agent/work/build/`, `agent/log.md`, the TOPO map, and captured agreements
   (`agent/raw/`, `agent/wiki/digests/`, `agent/wiki/people/`).
2. **If it IS agreed / by-design:** do NOT change working behaviour. Draft an explanation (for the
   reporter / ticket) citing *where and when* it was agreed. That context is the deliverable.
3. **If it is a genuine bug/gap:** proceed with investigate → root-cause → fix.
4. **If you cannot find a clear agreement either way:** say so, present what you found, and ask
   before assuming it is a bug.

---

## 6. Environment write policy & safety (MANDATORY)

**All bug fixes and implementation are done in the DEV environment ONLY.** Dev is the only
environment anything may WRITE to (schema changes, data create/update, flow edits, plugin deploys,
solution imports, connection changes, PCF pushes).

**UAT and Production are READ-ONLY.** Query them to review data, diagnose errors, or inspect state —
nothing more. Never run a write, deploy, or flow edit against UAT or Prod.

**Verify the connection BEFORE any environment-changing action.** Confirm the active connection /
`-EnvironmentUrl` targets the intended **Dev** environment and ABORT if it is anything else.
Repointing a CLI profile at a non-Dev environment for a read task is the classic near-miss — always
re-check the active profile before a write or push, and switch back to Dev first.

**If an unusual situation appears to require a change on a non-Dev environment, STOP and get explicit
human confirmation.** Prepare the exact command and hand it to a human to run — do not execute it
yourself. Promotion Dev → UAT → Prod happens only through the human-run release pipeline.

---

## 7. Branching & worktree discipline (MANDATORY)

This repo is often worked by **multiple concurrent AI/dev sessions sharing one clone**. A plain
`git checkout` moves `HEAD` for the whole clone and silently yanks other sessions onto that branch.
To prevent that, ticket work is isolated with **git worktrees**, and the main clone never changes
branch.

1. The **main clone stays on the current integration branch** (e.g. the active sprint branch). It is
   integration-only — never `git checkout` / branch-switch, never `git clean -fdx` from it.
2. **One worktree per ticket**, branched off the integration branch:
   ```bash
   git worktree add .worktrees/<KEY> -b feat/<KEY>-<short-desc> <integration-branch>
   ```
3. Do ALL of a ticket's work **inside its worktree folder** — edits, build, deploy, commits. Git
   attributes a change by the file's physical location, so scoped commits land on the ticket branch.
4. `.worktrees/` is gitignored. Provision build deps per worktree (`npm ci`, restore) — a fresh
   worktree has no `node_modules`.
5. **Merge back** to the integration branch when done and tested, then remove the worktree.
6. **Never** commit ticket work directly to the integration branch, to the default branch, or to
   another ticket's branch. If it is unclear which ticket work belongs to, ASK before starting.

Incidental repo-hygiene / process-doc fixes may be committed straight to the integration branch from
the main folder.

---

## 8. Core working principles

### Ask before assuming
When requirements are ambiguous, ask clarifying questions BEFORE implementing — multiple valid
approaches, unclear scope (ALL vs SPECIFIC), undefined error behaviour, or non-explicit intent.

### Analysis-first for complex logic
For complex business logic: write an analysis doc in `agent/work/analysis/` (current behaviour,
desired behaviour, all scenarios) → a test plan in `agent/work/testing/` → get approval → THEN
implement → append to `agent/log.md`.

### Never assume platform configuration
ALWAYS query live metadata (e.g. the Dataverse MCP `describe_table`) for field names, types, and
option-set values. Never hardcode or guess.

### No fossilised machine state — a validator is the source of truth
Never record machine/environment readiness in a committed config file (no "installed: yes" flags).
Probe it live each time — a stale positive is worse than no record, because it hides a regression.
The prerequisite lane validator (`agent-src/sync/Test-TemplatePrerequisites.ps1`) and the shared-tier
guard (`check-shared.ps1`) both PROBE rather than trust a stored answer; keep it that way.

### Enhance skills, never create temp scripts
A temp script solves a problem once; a skill update improves capability forever. When you hit a gap
in a skill: STOP, EXPLAIN the gap, PROPOSE an enhancement, and (after approval) implement it in the
skill — do not bypass it with a one-off `temp_*.ps1`.

### Keep comments and documentation accurate
A comment is a contract — it must match what the code or design actually does. Verify each comment
against the lines it describes before moving on; never leave a comment that does not match the code.

---

## 9. Problem-Solving Protocol (MANDATORY)

When you hit an unexpected error or issue: **STOP** → **EXPLAIN** what you observed and your
hypothesis → **PROPOSE** options with trade-offs → **WAIT** for approval before acting. Communicate
the root cause and why a change is needed before making it. The user is a decision-making partner,
not someone to inform after the fact.

**Do NOT:** create `temp_*.ps1` / one-off workarounds; silently try multiple approaches to "figure it
out"; edit skill code without first explaining the issue; act first and explain later.

---

## 10. Coding discipline (always apply)

Minimal complete change, surgical scope, verifiable done.

1. **Think before coding.** Surface assumptions and trade-offs; ask when scope or acceptance criteria
   are genuinely ambiguous; push back on riskier/more complex approaches.
2. **Simplicity first.** Walk the minimal-solution ladder (does it need to exist? stdlib? native
   platform? existing dependency/helper? small local change? only then custom code) and stop at the
   first rung that fully solves the task. Never simplify away validation, security, accessibility, or
   requested behaviour.
3. **Surgical changes.** Touch only what the task requires. Match existing style. Do not refactor
   unrelated code; mention unrelated issues separately.
4. **Goal-driven execution.** Define machine-checkable "done", reproduce → fix root cause → verify
   the same check passes. Read the full error/stack before diagnosing.
5. **Stop signals.** Kitchen-sink scope creep, wrong abstraction, happy-path-only at trust
   boundaries, runaway refactor — pause, re-scope to the smallest complete change, surface the
   trade-off.

---

## 11. Windows reserved filenames (CRITICAL)

**Never redirect output to `nul`** — it creates a real file with a reserved name that only `git bash
rm` can delete. Use `2>$null` (PowerShell) or `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue`. Avoid `CON`, `PRN`,
`AUX`, `NUL`, `COM1`-`COM9`, `LPT1`-`LPT9`.

---

## 12. Skills

Skills are specialised workflows under `.claude/skills/` (Claude) and `.github/skills/` (Copilot),
both generated from `agent-src/skills/{core,project}` by the sync. See
[`docs/onboarding/agent.md`](docs/onboarding/agent.md) for the full model and
[ADR-0008](docs/decisions/ADR-0008-agent-sync-mechanism.md) for the mechanism.

Key foundation / meta skills:

| Skill | Use when |
|---|---|
| **hso-template-architecture** | Before any development on a template-derived project — the layer/config/token map |
| **hso-architecture-map** | After creating/modifying/removing ANY component — update the TOPO map |
| **hso-skill-creator** | Creating a new skill (choose `--scope core\|project`) |
| **hso-skills-sync** | Verify skill parity across the generated tool directories |
| **hso-wiki-lint** | Enforce wiki invariants; regenerate `index.md` |
| **worklog** | Log a discrete piece of work for the timesheet, especially after a commit |

Domain skills (data modeling, plugins, form scripts, PCF, pipelines, Power Automate, wiki
ingest/capture/decision) live under the matching group. Reach a subject through its topic anchor in
`shared/dv/agent/wiki/topics/`.

---

## 13. Solutions folder & config are READ-ONLY / source-of-truth

- The `Solutions/` folder is the **output** of `pac solution export` — READ-ONLY. Never edit it, never
  `pac solution pack`/`import` to deploy. Change the platform directly via a skill, then re-run the
  export pipeline. Flow is one-way: **platform → export → `Solutions/`**.
- Per-project variability lives in the config blueprints
  (`ProjectTemplate/PipelinesHelpers/config/pipeline-defaults.json`,
  `solution-organizer.json`) — not hardcoded in files. See
  [ADR-0003](docs/decisions/ADR-0003-naming-and-token-contract.md).

---

## 14. Documentation updates & attribution

After implementing features: update `agent/wiki/system/` state, update the TOPO map, update component
READMEs, add a `agent/work/build/changelog/` entry, append to `agent/log.md`, and update
`agent/index.md` if pages were added.

Attribute all documentation and commits to the **human consultant** directing the work (per the local
config file), never to an AI assistant name.

---

## 15. Maintenance

Update **this file** (`AGENTS.md`) — never the generated `CLAUDE.md` / `copilot-instructions.md` — and
re-run `agent-src/sync/sync.ps1` when: adding solutions/components, changing build/deploy processes,
adding MCP servers, or making major architectural changes.
